author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Diagnose Bluetooth controller latency
summary: Use a repeatable input event, local display, and comparison connection to distinguish Bluetooth controller delay from frame pacing, audio routing, or radio interference.
heroAlt: Two 8BitDo Bluetooth gamepads photographed together for a wireless controller latency comparison

sourceLabels.android-controller-events: Android button, axis, and device event guidance

blocks.text: Measure input, picture, and sound as separate delays

Choose a button action with an immediate visual change and test on the phone display with local speakers. Record high-frame-rate video containing the physical button and screen so press-to-photon delay can be counted frame by frame. Disable Bluetooth audio, external displays, and variable test scenes before comparing the wireless controller with a wired or known-low-latency input path.

Do not estimate controller delay from sound timing or a television image. Bluetooth headphones and display processing add independent latency, while unstable emulation speed can delay every input source. Keep the game scene, frame rate, display route, and camera recording rate unchanged; otherwise a smaller number cannot be attributed to the controller link.

items: Controller fully charged and paired without a second duplicate entry.
Phone display fixed to one refresh mode for the comparison.
Bluetooth headphones disconnected during the first visual-input test.
Film at least twenty physical presses and screen responses at a known camera rate, with Bluetooth audio and external display paths removed.
Repeat the identical visual action over a wired path so radio delay can be separated from game logic, frame delivery, and panel response.
1. Choose a menu cursor or immediate jump action that can be repeated safely.
2. Record several physical presses and visual responses with the local phone display.
3. Note whether delay is constant or arrives as occasional clusters.
4. Move Wi-Fi and other Bluetooth traffic away for one controlled comparison.
5. Connect the same controller through supported USB if available, without changing its PS2 mapping.
6. Repeat the identical action, camera position, and frame-rate conditions.
7. Reconnect Bluetooth and test after clearing only stale duplicate pairing entries.
8. Keep the result as a device-specific note instead of applying a global timing hack.

blocks.text: Measure at least twenty presses and inspect both the median and the spread. A constant offset suggests transport or presentation delay; occasional long gaps or several inputs arriving together indicate radio interference, power saving, or scheduling bursts. Compare the same controller wired, then repeat Bluetooth beside and away from other 2.4 GHz traffic.

The wireless result passes when repeated presses have a narrow distribution, no burst delivery, and a stable difference from the wired control. Repeat after the controller sleeps and reconnects, and again after the phone resumes from the background. Save the videos and frame counts rather than reporting a single subjective impression.

items: Visual timing is judged independently from Bluetooth audio.
The comparison uses the same game scene and rendering load.
Repeated presses show a stable distribution rather than one anecdotal event.
Store every press-to-photon count and report median plus spread; burst delivery is visible in the distribution, not a single best sample.
Let the controller sleep, reconnect it, and repeat the measurement after a cold app start without changing game, display, or recording setup.

blocks.text: Delays that do not originate in the controller

items: Both wired and wireless inputs slow in one scene: investigate emulation speed or frame pacing.
Picture reacts promptly but sound is late: diagnose the audio route.
Only an external screen is late: compare the phone panel and display processing.
Inputs arrive in bursts near other radios: repeat under reduced interference.

blocks.text: Return to the original wireless profile

Restore original radio and power settings one at a time while preserving the known-good game and display configuration. Remove experimental pairings, forget only the test device if necessary, and reapply its documented profile after pairing. Do not reset Wi-Fi, clear all Bluetooth devices, or change emulator timing merely to improve one uncontrolled measurement.
Bluetooth delay varies by the entire radio path

Observed latency combines controller scan rate, Bluetooth scheduling, emulator input sampling, game logic, frame delivery, and panel response. The procedure isolates several layers but does not produce a universal number for that controller model. Report phone, Android build, connection mode, game scene, sample count, and distribution with every result.
